newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended up in the same positive mood that lifted other major bond markets after a slightly weaker-than-expected U.S. September NAPM.
After a sharp drop in the 10-year yield under 8.00 percent in a morning Treasury auction, dealers forecast further easing at Wednesday's auction of five- and 15-year bonds.
"I do expect bigger demand for the five-year bonds," a dealer with a Spanish house said.
But the market is focused primarily on Thursday's Bank of Spain repo, which is tipped to lower the official key money market rate now at 7.25 percent.

"I think Wednesday we will face a range trading day, with futures between support at 106.40 and resistance at 106.80," a Madrid dealer said. He said he expects the central bank to cut the repo rate by 50 basis points "without posing any danger."
He added: "They have enough room. The spread over 10-year German Bunds is at 183 bp while the differential over the overnight rates is at around 425 bp."
Others suggested the Bank of Spain could take a more cautious approach before September CPI due next week.
Mibor December contract on 90-day interbank deposits closed unchanged at 93.32. -- Madrid newsroom + 341 585 2160
